next_step: Finalize POC performance report and pricing; legal to review DPA; schedule exec review wk of 2026-03-10
notes: Acct background: mid-market SaaS (B2B customer support platform). Highly chat-centric product; user-facing agents rely on low tail latency.
Initial interest: migration from current LLM API provider due to repeated latency regressions in streaming APIs (timeouts and poor tail behavior).
Primary ask: hosted API to get live quickly (low-friction), then Dedicated for production traffic to guarantee throughput & SLA.
Workload: multi-turn agent flows + tool-calls (internal ticketing, customer DB lookups). Need streaming responses with token-level progress to UI.
Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency < 150ms for typical agent flows; cold-starts up to 300ms acceptable. Throughput target: 200 concurrent agents peak.
Cost sensitivity: mid (startup economics) but willing to pay reserved capacity for predictable perf; ARR expectation $100-300k.
Model prefs: open model lineage preferred; will accept small finetuned/repacked model variants. Interested in quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
Security: must pass SOC2 + SSO/SAML + audit logs; eventual requirement for VPC/Dedicated deployment for sensitive customers.
Incumbent provider: currently on X-provider (custom streaming) - started seeing regressions late 2025 causing user complaints and 3 incidents.
Benchmarking ask: compare Redwood streaming vs incumbent on tail latency, connection stability, and tool-calling reliability (webhook/LLM tool flows).
POC setup: ran 3 benchmark scenarios (short-turn response, long-turn streaming with tool calls, concurrent agent ramp). Redwood assigned test harness and provided kernel/quantization notes.

Bench results (summary): Redwood shows ~30-45% improvement in 95/99 p-tail latency vs incumbent in our synthetic runs; streaming stability improved (fewer truncated streams), tool-calls success rate 98% vs incumbent 92%.
AE notes: ConvoFlow team happy with demo UX (streaming + function/tool calling) - product team liked the ability to attach structured outputs and retry/fallback policies.
SE notes: need to validate KV-cache behavior across multi-turn sessions; recommended Dedicated setup with autoscale burst for peak loads.
Security review: intake form submitted 2026-02-05; Redwood sent security FAQ and SOC2 attestation. Security follow-up on data residency for EU customers.
Pricing: requested committed capacity quote for 2x expected peak (safety buffer). Redwood provided draft pricing + commitment options; negotiation ongoing.
Customer quote: 'We saw fewer dropped streams and more consistent latency on Redwood during the demo - that drove exec interest.'
Decision criteria: latency SLO adherence, predictable cost under burst, security sign-off, legal DPA, ease of migration (SDKs + data mapping), Dedicated SLA.
Risks: procurement timeline, legal signoff on DPA clauses, EU data residency questions for subset of enterprise customers.
Preference: move to Hosted API quickly to validate in prod with limited traffic; migrate hot-path to Dedicated once SLA and residency confirmed.
Next internal milestone: exec review and procurement approval targeted for April 2026.
